label: main-tor
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{main-tor} Let $(A,\mathfrak{m} )$ be a dominant Cohen-Macaulay \ local ring of dimension
$d$ and let $I$ be an $\mathfrak{m} $-primary ideal of $A$. Assume the residue field of $A$ is infinite. Let $N$ be a perfect $A$-module of dimension $t \geq 1$.  Let $M$ be a non-free MCM $A$-module. Then we have
 $\limsup_{j \rightarrow \infty} r_{I, N}^j(M) = r_{I,N}^2(\operatorname{Syz}^d_A(k))$.
head: environment

label: main-ext
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{main-ext} Let $(A,\mathfrak{m} )$ be a dominant Cohen-Macaulay \ local ring of dimension
$d$ and let $I$ be an $\mathfrak{m} $-primary ideal of $A$.  Assume the residue field of $A$ is infinite. Let $V$ be a Cohen-Macaulay \ $A$-module of dimension $t \geq 1$ and of finite injective dimension. Let $M$ be a non-free MCM $A$-module.  Then we have
 $\limsup_{j \rightarrow \infty} s_{I, V}^j(M) = s_{I,V}^1(\operatorname{Syz}^d_A(k))$.

label: rach-prop
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{rach-prop} (with setup as in \ref{rachel}). Let $M$ be a finitely generated $A$-module. Let $E$ be a graded $\mathcal{R} $-module. Then
\begin{enumerate}[\rm (1)]
  \item The $A$-modules $\operatorname{Tor}^A_i(M, E)$ and $\operatorname{Ext}_A^i(M, E)$ are graded $\mathcal{R} $-modules for all $i \geq 0$.
\item If $E = \bigoplus_{n \in \mathbb{Z} } E_n$ then $\operatorname{Tor}^A_i(M, E) = \bigoplus_{n \in \mathbb{Z} } \operatorname{Tor}^A_i(M, E_n)$ and $\operatorname{Ext}_A^i(M, E) = \bigoplus_{n \in \mathbb{Z} }\operatorname{Ext}^i_A(M, E_n)$ for all $i \geq 0$.
  \item If $E$ is a finitely generated $\mathcal{R} $-module then $\operatorname{Tor}^A_i(M, E)$ and $\operatorname{Ext}_A^i(M, E)$ are finitely generated  $\mathcal{R} $-modules for all $i \geq 0$.
  \item Let $0 \rightarrow E^\prime \rightarrow E \rightarrow E^{\prime \prime} \rightarrow 0$ be an exact sequence of $\mathcal{R} (I)$-modules. Then it induces an  exact sequence of graded $\mathcal{R} $-modules
  \begin{enumerate}[\rm (a)]
    \item  \begin{align*}
           \cdots    &\rightarrow\operatorname{Tor}^A_i(M, E^\prime) \rightarrow \operatorname{Tor}^A_i(M, E) \rightarrow \operatorname{Tor}^A_i(M, E^{\prime, \prime}) \\
             &\rightarrow \operatorname{Tor}^A_{i-1}(M, E^\prime) \rightarrow \cdots
           \end{align*}
\item  \begin{align*}
           \cdots    &\rightarrow\operatorname{Ext}_A^i(M, E^\prime) \rightarrow \operatorname{Ext}_A^i(M, E) \rightarrow \operatorname{Ext}_A^i(M, E^{\prime, \prime}) \\
             &\rightarrow \operatorname{Ext}_A^{i+1}(M, E^\prime) \rightarrow \cdots
           \end{align*}
  \end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}\qed
head: environment

label: bella
title: Proposition
body_md: \label{bella}(with hypotheses as in \ref{rachel}) Further assume $A$ is \\ Cohen-Macaulay and $I$ is a proper ideal of $A$. Let $U, V$ be finitely generated $A$-modules with $\operatorname{projdim} U$ and $\operatorname{injdim} V$ finite. Then $\operatorname{Tor}^A_i(M, L^I(U))$ and \\ $\operatorname{Ext}^i_A(M, L^I(V))$ are finitely generated $\mathcal{R} $-modules for all $i > d$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We have an exact sequence of $\mathcal{R} $-modules $0 \rightarrow U[It] \rightarrow U[t] \rightarrow L^I(U)(-1) \rightarrow 0$. We note that $\operatorname{Tor}^A_i(M, U[t]) = \bigoplus_{n \geq 0}\operatorname{Tor}^A_i(M, U)  = 0$ for $i > d$.
  We apply $M \otimes -$ to this exact sequence.
  It follows that
  $\operatorname{Tor}^A_i(M, L^I(U)(-1)) \cong \operatorname{Tor}^A_{i -1}(M, U[It])$ for $i \geq d +2$ as $\mathcal{R} $-modules and  $\operatorname{Tor}^A_{d+1}(M, L^I(U)(-1)) $ is an $\mathcal{R} $-submodule of $\operatorname{Tor}^A_{d}(M, U[It])$. So
  $\operatorname{Tor}^A_i(M, L^I(U))$  are finitely generated $\mathcal{R} $-modules for all $i > d$, see \ref{rach-prop}..

  We have an exact sequence of $\mathcal{R} $-modules $0 \rightarrow V[It] \rightarrow V[t] \rightarrow L^I(V)(-1) \rightarrow 0$. We note that $\operatorname{Ext}_A^i(M, V[t]) = \bigoplus_{n \geq 0}\operatorname{Ext}_A^i(M, V)  = 0$ for $i > d$.
  We apply $\operatorname{Hom}_A(M,  -)$ to this exact sequence.
  It follows that
  $\operatorname{Ext}_A^i(M, L^I(V)(-1)) \cong \operatorname{Ext}_A^{i +1}(M, V[It])$ for $i \geq d +1$.
  So $\operatorname{Ext}_A^i(M, L^I(V))$
    are finitely generated $\mathcal{R} $-modules for all $i > d$, see \ref{rach-prop}..
head: environment

label: complex
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{complex}(\cite[Proposition 3]{Theo}):
Let $(A, \mathfrak{m} )$ be  a Noetherian local ring. Let $\mathcal{C} \colon F_2 \rightarrow F_1 \rightarrow F_0$ be a complex with $F_1, F_0$ finitely generated $A$-modules. Let
$N$ be another finitely generated $A$-module and let $I$ be an ideal of $A$.
Assume $H_1(\mathcal{C} \otimes N/I^nN)$ has finite length for all $n \geq 1$. Then
\begin{enumerate}[\rm (1)]
  \item The function $n \rightarrow \ell(H_1(\mathcal{C} \otimes N/I^n N))$ of polynomial type, say of degree $u_N$.
  \item We have $u_N \leq \max \{ \dim H_1(\mathcal{C} \otimes N), \lambda_N(I) -1 \}$.
  \item If $\dim H_1(\mathcal{C} \otimes N)\geq \lambda_N(I) $ then the inequality in $\rm{(2)}$ becomes an equality.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

label: tor-ext-deg
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{tor-ext-deg}(\cite[Corollary 4]{Theo}:) Let $(A, \mathfrak{m} )$ be  a Noetherian local ring. Let $M, N$ be finitely generated $A$-modules and let $I$ be an ideal in $A$. Fix $i \geq 0$.
\begin{enumerate}[\rm (I)]
  \item Assume $\ell(\operatorname{Tor}^A_i(M, N/I^n N))$ is finite for all $n \geq 1$. Then
  \begin{enumerate}[\rm (i)]
    \item The function $n \rightarrow \ell(\operatorname{Tor}^A_i(M, N/I^n N))$ is of polynomial type say of degree $t_I(M, N)$.
    \item $t_I(M, N) \leq \max \{ \dim \operatorname{Tor}^A_i(M, N), \lambda_N(I) - 1\}$.
    \item If $\dim \operatorname{Tor}^A_i(M, N) \geq \lambda_N(I)$ then the inequality in $\rm{(ii)}$ becomes an equality.
  \end{enumerate}
  \item Assume $\ell(\operatorname{Ext}^i_A(M, N/I^n N))$ is finite for all $n \geq 1$. Then
  \begin{enumerate}[\rm (i)]
    \item The function $n \rightarrow \ell(\operatorname{Ext}^i_A(M, N/I^n N))$ is of polynomial type say of degree $e_I(M, N)$.
    \item $e_I(M, N) \leq \max \{ \dim \operatorname{Ext}^i_A(M, N), \lambda_N(I) - 1\}$.
    \item If $\dim \operatorname{Ext}^i_A(M, N) \geq \lambda_N(I)$ then the inequality in $\rm{(ii)}$ becomes an equality.
  \end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}

label: mod-filter-sup
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{mod-filter-sup}(with setup as in \ref{setup}). We have
\begin{enumerate}[\rm (1)]
  \item Fix $j_0 \geq d + 3$. Assume $t \geq 2$. Then
  there exists $x \in I$ which is $I$-superficial with respect to  \ $N$ and $xt$ is $\operatorname{Tor}^A_j(M, L^I(N))$-filter regular  for $j = d +1,\ldots, j_0$.
   Set $\overline{N} = N/x N$. Note $\overline{N}$ is perfect of dimension $t -1$. In particular we have exact sequences for $j = d+2, \ldots, j_0$ and $n \gg 0$
      $$ 0 \rightarrow \operatorname{Tor}^A_j(M, N/I^n N) \rightarrow \operatorname{Tor}^A_j(M, N/I^{n + 1} N) \rightarrow \operatorname{Tor}^A_j(M, \overline{N}/I^{n+1}\overline{N}) \rightarrow 0.$$
  \item Fix $j_0 \geq d + 2$. Assume $v \geq 2$. Then there exists $y \in I$ which is $I$-superficial with respect to  \ $V$ and $yt$ is $\operatorname{Ext}_A^j(M, L^I(V))$-filter regular  for $j = d +1,\ldots, j_0 + 1$. Set $\overline{V} = V/y V$. Note $\overline{V}$ is Cohen-Macaulay \ of dimension $t-1$ and of finite injective dimension. In particular we have exact sequences for $j = d+1, \ldots, j_0$ and $n \gg 0$
      $$ 0 \rightarrow \operatorname{Ext}_A^j(M, V/I^n V) \rightarrow \operatorname{Ext}_A^j(M, V/I^{n + 1} V) \rightarrow \operatorname{Ext}_A^j(M, \overline{V}/I^{n+1}\overline{V}) \rightarrow 0.$$
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
(1) By \ref{bella},  $\operatorname{Tor}^A_i(M, L^I(N))$ are finitely generated $\mathcal{R} $-modules for all $i > d$. By \ref{lila}  there exists $x \in I$ which is $I$-superficial with respect to  \ $N$ and $xt$ is $\operatorname{Tor}^A_j(M, L^I(N))$-filter regular  for $j = d +1,\ldots, j_0$. As $N$ is Cohen-Macaulay \ of positive dimension we get that $x$ is $N$-regular and $(I^{n+1}N \colon x) = I^nN$ for $n \gg 0$. say $n \geq n_0$.  We have an exact sequence of $\mathcal{R} $-modules
 \[
 0 \rightarrow \bigoplus_{n = 0}^{n_0 -1}\frac{(I^{n+1}N \colon x)}{I^nN} \rightarrow L^I(N)(-1) \xrightarrow{xt} L^I(N) \rightarrow L^I(\overline{N}) \rightarrow 0.
 \]
This induces short exact sequences for $n \geq n_0$
\[
0 \rightarrow N/I^{n}N \xrightarrow{\alpha_n} N/I^{n + 1}N  \xrightarrow{\rho_n} \overline{N}/I^{n+1}\overline{N} \rightarrow 0.
\]
Therefor for $n \geq n_0$ we have an exact sequence for all $j$
$$ \rightarrow \operatorname{Tor}^A_j(M, N/I^{n}N) \xrightarrow{\alpha_n^j(M)} \operatorname{Tor}^A_j(M, N/I^{n + 1}N)\xrightarrow{\rho_n^j(M)} \operatorname{Tor}^A_j(M, \overline{N}/I^{n + 1}\overline{N}) \rightarrow  $$
Here $\alpha_n^j(M) = \operatorname{Tor}^A_j(M, \alpha_n)$ and $\rho_n^j(M) = \operatorname{Tor}^A_j(M, \rho_n)$.
We note that $\alpha_n^j$ is nothing but the $n^{th}$ component of the map $\operatorname{Tor}^A_j(M, L^I(N))(-1) \xrightarrow{xt} \operatorname{Tor}^A_j(M, L^I(N))$ and so is injective for $j = d+ 1, \ldots, j_0$ and $n \gg 0$ as  $xt$ is $\operatorname{Tor}^A_j(M, L^I(N))$-filter regular  for $j = d +1,\ldots, j_0$.
It follows that for $j  =  d+2, \ldots, j_0$ and $n \gg 0$
we have exact sequences
      $$ 0 \rightarrow \operatorname{Tor}^A_j(M, N/I^n N) \rightarrow \operatorname{Tor}^A_j(M, N/I^{n + 1} N) \rightarrow \operatorname{Tor}^A_j(M, \overline{N}/I^{n+1}\overline{N}) \rightarrow 0.$$

(2)  By \ref{bella}, $\operatorname{Ext}^i_A(M, L^I(V))$ are finitely generated $\mathcal{R} $-modules for all $i > d$. By \ref{lila}  there exists $x \in I$ which is $I$-superficial with respect to  \ $V$ and $xt$ is $\operatorname{Ext}_A^j(M, L^I(U))$-filter regular  for $j = d +1,\ldots, j_0 + 1$. Rest of the arguments are similar to (1).

title: Proof
body_md:
(1) We prove the result by induction on $t = \dim N$. Fix $j_0 \geq d + 2$.
By \ref{setup} we have $r_{I, N}^{j}(k) = -1 $ or zero for all $j \geq d + 1$.
By \ref{fin-dim}(1) it follows that $r_{I, N}^{j_0}(k) = -1 $ if and only if $r_{I, N}^{d + 2}(k) = -1$ if and only if $\operatorname{projdim} A/I^n$ is finite for all $n \gg 0$.
The assertion follows when $t = 1$.

Now assume that $\dim N = t \geq 2$ and the assertion holds for all perfect modules $L$ of dimension  $t - 1$. By \ref{fin-dim}(1) it follows that $r_{I, N}^{j_0}(k) = -1 $ if and only if $r_{I, N}^{d + 2}(k) = -1$. So assume that $\operatorname{projdim} N/I^nN = \infty$ for all $n \gg 0$. Thus $r_{I, N}^j(k) \geq 0$ for all $j \geq d + 1$. By \ref{mod-filter-sup}(1)
it follows that there exists $x$ an $I$-superficial sequence with respect to \ $N$ such that $xt$ is $\operatorname{Tor}^A_j(M, L^I(N))$-filter regular  for $j = d +1,\ldots, j_0$. Note $\overline{N} = N/xN$ is perfect $A$-module of dimension $t-1$. By the exact sequence in \ref{mod-filter-sup}(1) we get that $r_{I,N}^{j_0}(k) = r_{I, \overline{N}}^{j_0}(k) + 1$ and $r_{I, N}^{d+2}(k) = r_{I, \overline{N}}^{d+2}(k) + 1$. The result follows by induction.

(2) This can be proved on the same lines as (1). We have to use \ref{fin-dim}(2)  and \ref{mod-filter-sup}(2).

title: Proof
body_md:
(1) Fix $j_0 \geq d + 2$
We note that we have nothing to show if $r_{I, N}^{j_0}(M) = -1$. Also if $r_{I, N}^{j_0}(M) \geq 0$ then necessarily $\operatorname{projdim} N/I^{n+1}N = \infty$ for all $n \gg 0$. So $r_{I,N}^{d+2}(k) \geq 0$.
This proves the result when $\dim N = 1$ as the possible degrees are $-1$ and $0$, see \ref{setup}.  We prove the result by induction on $t = \dim N$. The case $t = 1$ holds as discussed before. Now assume $\dim N = t \geq 2$ and the result is known for perfect modules of dimension $t-1$. We will assume that $r_{I, N}^{j_0}(M) \geq 0$ as otherwise we have nothing to show. It follows that $\operatorname{projdim} N/I^{n+1}N = \infty$ for all $n \gg 0$. So $r_{I,N}^{d+2}(k) \geq 0$. We may choose $x$ which is $I$-superficial with respect to \ $N$ and $xt$ is $\operatorname{Tor}^A_j(M, L^I(N))$-filter regular  for $j = d +1,\ldots, j_0$, Furthermore we can also assume that $xt$ is $\operatorname{Tor}^A_j(k, L^I(N))$-filter regular  for $j = d +1, d+2$. Note $\overline{N} = N/xN$ is perfect of dimension $t-1$. By the exact sequence in \ref{mod-filter-sup}(1) we get that $r_{I,N}^{j_0}(M) = r_{I, \overline{N}}^{j_0}(M) + 1$ and $r_{I, N}^{d+2}(k) = r_{I, \overline{N}}^{d+2}(k) + 1$. The result follows by induction.

(2) This can be proved on the same lines as (1). We have to use \ref{fin-dim}(2)  and \ref{mod-filter-sup}(2).

label: iso
title: Proposition
body_md:
(with setup as above)
\label{iso} Let $\mathbf{X}, \mathbf{Y} \in \mathcal{K} ^{-,b}(\operatorname{proj} A)$. If $\mathbf{X} \cong \mathbf{Y}$ then for all $i \in \mathbb{Z} $ and for all $n \geq 0$ we have isomorphism of complexes
\begin{enumerate}[\rm (1)]
  \item  $\mathbf{X} \otimes N/I^{n+1}N \cong \mathbf{Y} \otimes N/I^{n+1}N$.
  \item $\operatorname{Hom}_A(\mathbf{X}, V/I^{n+1}V) \cong \operatorname{Hom}_A(\mathbf{Y}, V/I^{n+1}V)$
\end{enumerate}

label: triangle
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{triangle}
 (with setup as above)
 Let $\mathbf{X}, \mathbf{Y}, \mathbf{Z} \in \mathcal{K} ^{-,b}(\operatorname{proj} A)$.
  Assume we have a triangle $\mathbf{X} \xrightarrow{f} \mathbf{Y} \rightarrow \mathbf{Z} \rightarrow \mathbf{X}[-1]$ in $\mathcal{K} ^{-,b}(\operatorname{proj} A)$.Then
\begin{enumerate}[\rm (1)]
\item For all $i \in \mathbb{Z} $  and for all $n \geq 0$ we have a long exact sequence in homology
\begin{align*}
  \cdots  &\rightarrow  H_i(\mathbf{X}\otimes N/I^{n+1}N) \rightarrow  H_i(\mathbf{Y}\otimes N/I^{n+1}N)  \rightarrow  H_i(\mathbf{Z}\otimes N/I^{n+1}N)  \\
  &\rightarrow  H_{i-1}(\mathbf{X}\otimes N/I^{n+1}N) \rightarrow \cdots
\end{align*}
  \item For all $i \in \mathbb{Z} $ we have
  $$\alpha_{I, N}^i(\mathbf{Y}) \leq \max\{ \alpha_{I, N}^i(\mathbf{X}),  \alpha_{I, N}^i(\mathbf{Z})\}.$$
  \item  We have
  $$\alpha_{I, N}(\mathbf{Y}) \leq \max\{ \alpha_{I, N}(\mathbf{X}),  \alpha_{I, N}(\mathbf{Z})\}.$$
  \item  For all $i \in \mathbb{Z} $  and for all $n \geq 1$ we have a long exact sequence in cohomology
\begin{align*}
  \cdots  &\rightarrow  H^i(\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf{Z}, V/I^{n}V)) \rightarrow  H^i(\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf{Y}, V/I^{n}V))  \rightarrow  H^i(\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf{X}, V/I^{n}V))  \\
  &\rightarrow H^{i+1}(\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf{Z}, V/I^{n}V))\rightarrow \cdots
\end{align*}
  \item For all $i \in \mathbb{Z} $ we have
  $$\beta_{I, V}^i(\mathbf{Y}) \leq \max\{ \beta_{I, V}^i(\mathbf{X}),  \beta_{I, V}^i(\mathbf{Z})\}.$$
  \item  We have
  $$\beta_{I, V}(\mathbf{Y}) \leq \max\{ \beta_{I, V}(\mathbf{X}),  \beta_{I, V}(\mathbf{Z})\}.$$
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
(1) Set $\mathbf{Z}^\prime = \operatorname{cone}(f)$. We note that $\mathbf{Z} \cong \mathbf{Z}^\prime$. We have a short exact sequence of complexes $0 \rightarrow \mathbf{Y} \rightarrow \mathbf{Z}^\prime \rightarrow \mathbf{X}[-1] \rightarrow 0$. As all the modules involved are free we get an exact sequence of complexes for all $m \geq 0$,
   $$  0 \rightarrow \mathbf{Y}\otimes N/I^{n+1}N \rightarrow \mathbf{Z}^\prime\otimes N/I^{n+1}N \rightarrow \mathbf{X}\otimes N/I^{n+1}N[-1] \rightarrow 0.  $$
The long exact sequence in homology and Proposition \ref{iso} gives the result.

(2) This follows from (1).

(3)  This follows from (2).

(4) This is similar to (1).

(5) This follows from (4).

(6)  This follows from (5).

label: mom
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{mom}
(with setup as above)
Let $\mathbf{X}, \mathbf{Y}, \mathbf{Z} \in \mathcal{K} ^{-,b}(\operatorname{proj} A)$. Set $\mathcal{D} _{sg} = \mathcal{D} _{sg}(A)$
\begin{enumerate}[\rm (1)]
  \item If $\mathbf{X} \cong \mathbf{Y}$ in $\mathcal{D} _{sg}$ then
  \begin{enumerate}[\rm (a)]
    \item $         \alpha_{I, N}(\mathbf{X}) =   \alpha_{I, N}(\mathbf{Y})$.
    \item  $\beta_{I, V}(\mathbf{X}) =   \beta_{I, V}(\mathbf{Y})        $

  \end{enumerate}
  \item  Assume we have a triangle $s \colon \mathbf{X} \rightarrow \mathbf{Y} \rightarrow \mathbf{Z} \rightarrow \mathbf{X}[-1]$ in $\mathcal{D} _{sg}$. Then
\begin{enumerate}[\rm (a)]
  \item $$\alpha_{I, N}(\mathbf{Y}) \leq \max\{ \alpha_{I, N}(\mathbf{X}),  \alpha_{I, N}(\mathbf{Z})\}.$$
  \item  $$\beta_{I, V}(\mathbf{Y}) \leq \max\{ \beta_{I, V}(\mathbf{X}),  \beta_{I, V}(\mathbf{Z})\}.$$
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}

title: Proof
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $M$ be a non-free MCM $A$-module. Let $\mathbf{P}$ be the minimal projective resolution of $M$. Then $\mathbf{P} \neq 0$ in $\mathcal{D} _{sg}$. Let $\mathbf{Q}$ be the minimal free resolution of $k$.
As $A$ is dominant we get that $\mathbf{Q} \in \operatorname{thick}(\mathbf{P})$.
Set $r = \limsup_{j \rightarrow \infty} r_{I, N}^j(M)$. We have $\alpha_{I, N}(\mathbf{P}) = r$.

We now recall the definition of thick closure of $\mathbf{P}$.
We note that $\alpha_{I, N}(\mathbf{X}[m]) = \alpha_{I, N}(\mathbf{X}) $ for all $m \in \mathbb{Z} $. Also $\alpha_{I, N}(\mathbf{X}) \leq \alpha_{I, N}(\mathbf{X} \oplus \mathbf{Y})$.
If $\mathbf{X} \rightarrow \mathbf{Y} \rightarrow \mathbf{Z} \rightarrow \mathbf{X}[-1]$ is a triangle in $\mathcal{D} _{sg}$ with  $\alpha_{I, N}(\mathbf{X}) \leq r$ and $\alpha_{I, N}(\mathbf{Z}) \leq r$ then by \ref{mom}(2)(a) we get $\alpha_{I, N}(\mathbf{Y}) \leq r$.
So we get $\alpha_{I, N}(\mathbf{X}) \leq r$ for all $\mathbf{X} \in \operatorname{thick}(\mathbf{P})$. As $A$ is dominant we get $\mathbf{Q} \in \operatorname{thick}(\mathbf{P})$. So  $\alpha_{I, N}(\mathbf{Q}) \leq r$. By \ref{equi-residue}, we get $r_{I, N}^2(\Omega^d(k)) = \alpha_{I, N}(\mathbf{Q})$  But by \ref{bound} we get $r \leq r_{I, N}^2(\Omega^d(k)) $. It follows that $r =  r_{I, N}^2(\Omega^d(k))$.
